newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foreign firms buy one-third of Russian TSUM shares. [CORRECTED]
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms buy one-third of Russian TSUM shares. [CORRECTED]

text.p: Foreign companies hold one-third of the authorised capital of one of Russia's biggest retailers, OAO Torgovy Dom TSUM after a heavily oversubscribed public share placement, the lead manager of the issue said on Thursday.
Investment company OLMA President Oleg Yachnik also told a news conference that it was preparing a public placement of level one American Depositary Receipts for TSUM.
"All one hundred percent of shares found their shareholders," Yachnik said.

Most shareholders acquired less than five percent of the $10.83 million issue, he said, adding the only investor with more than a five percent package was the AIG-Brunswick Millenium Fund, set up by American International Group Inc (AIG) and Brunswick Capital Management Ltd. (Corrects name of shareholder from "the Millenium Fund, managed by ING-Brunswick Capital Management" to "AIG-Brunswick Millenium Fund").
Other buyers were Templeton and US-Russia Investment Fund, Yachnik said.

Jacques Der Megrditchian, deputy chief executive at Societe Generale Vostok, an agent of the placement, said other foreign buyers included France's Caisse des Depots, insurance company Groupe Victoire, Compagnie Financiere Rotschild and Societe Generale's branch Societe Generale European Emerging Asset Management.
One of Russia's biggest banks, Agroprombank, Yunibest bank and OLMA-bank also bought shares, Yachnik said.
Under the placement, launched on October 1, TSUM offered 30 million shares at 2,000 roubles (36 cents) each and the issue was 50 percent oversubscribed, Yachnik said.
TSUM became the first prominent Russian company to launch a share issue to raise funds for further development of its operations.
The funds raised during the issue will help finance a $22 million reconstruction project with the rest of the money coming from bank loans and TSUM's cash flow.
Alexander Voskoboinikov, TSUM's chief executive, forecast 1996 turnover would rise to 200 billion roubles from 174 billion roubles in 1995 with a goal to reach 400 billion in 1997.
TSUM's charter capital is now 89.6 billion roubles, Yachnik said.
TSUM closed at $0.361 on December 16, when it was last traded.
